MegaMemory fork

Persistent project knowledge graph for coding agents — multilingual, token-economical, visible in the UI.

> **Fork of [0xK3vin/MegaMemory](https://github.com/0xK3vin/MegaMemory) v1.6.2 (MIT).** > Fork of the npm package [`megamemory`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/megamemory), published as `@bloodyeagle/megamemory`. > Upstream keeps the concept, this fork fixes multilingual IDs, adds hybrid search, > a context budget, fact freshness, digests, export and token accounting. > Русская версия: [README.ru.md](./README.ru.md). An [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server that lets your coding agent build and query a graph of concepts, architecture, and decisions — so it **remembers across sessions**. The LLM is the indexer. No AST parsing, no static analysis: the agent reads code, writes concepts in its own words, and queries them before future tasks. The graph stores **concepts** — features, modules, patterns, decisions — not code symbols. Everything persists in a per-project SQLite database at `.megamemory/knowledge.db`. --- ## What this fork changes | Area | Upstream 1.6.2 | This fork | |---|---|---| | Node IDs | slug strips everything outside `[a-z0-9-]`; Cyrillic, CJK, Greek, emoji names collapse to `""` and the second such node is lost | Unicode-safe slug: letters of any script, diacritics stripped only after Latin/Cyrillic/Greek/Hebrew bases (katakana dakuten and Hangul jamo are preserved), `/` becomes `-`, NFC output, hash fallback for emoji-only names, `-` on collisions | | Embeddings | `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`, English-only, dimension hardcoded | `Xenova/multilingual-e5-small` by default (`MEGAMEMORY_EMBED_MODEL`), e5 `passage:`/`query:` prefixes, dimension read from the model, vector search disabled on model mismatch until `megamemory reembed` | | Search | cosine similarity only | hybrid: FTS5 + vector fused with RRF, per-hit `via: vector \| fts \| both`, query sanitization for `MATCH`, short-CJK routing, optional trigram index, `name_norm` LIKE fallback | | Context | `understand` returns everything it found | `mode: "compact"` by default, bounded by `max_tokens` (1500), summaries trimmed to 240 chars, edges between returned nodes only, `meta.returned / dropped / tokens_estimated`; the answer ends with a `next` action block (`must_read` / `skip` / `followups` / `record`) | | Freshness | delete or nothing | node `status` (`active`/`superseded`/`deprecated`), `supersedes` and `contradicts` edges, outdated nodes hidden from answers but visible in the graph; facts expire: `valid_until` drops state claims out of answers after their date | | Duplicates | manual merge | `megamemory consolidate` finds embedding-similar pairs (≥ 0.95) and merges them with edge transfer | | Long modules | every child read separately | `digest` nodes: one per module, rebuilt after the 5th child, lower search weight | | Portability | DB only | `megamemory export --md ` writes one markdown file per node (frontmatter + wiki-links), `--check` for CI | | Cost visibility | none | every `understand` / `list_roots` / `get_concept` is measured; 7-day aggregates in `megamemory stats`, `/api/stats` and the explorer's **Tokens** panel; `megamemory stats --funnel` measures the understand → follow-up → record funnel over the `timeline` journal (`--json` for scripts) | | Migration | — | `megamemory migrate --dry-run/--apply` upgrades an upstream database in place, additively, with backups and a downgrade-safe schema | --- ## The loop `understand → work → update` 1. **Session start** — the agent calls `list_roots` (budgeted) to orient itself. 2. **Before a task** — `understand` with a natural-language query, or `get_concept` for an exact ID. 3. **Follow relevant `next` instructions** — read `must_read` refs, run ready-made `followups`, and record per `record` after the change. Refs and a brief without the claim do not prove whole-file coverage; `skip` does not replace checking current code. All modes use the actual MCP wire budget and refuse an impossible required envelope. 4. **After a task** — `create_concept` / `update_concept`, then `link` for relationships. --- ## Provenance Decisions are only as good as their sources. The graph keeps that linkage explicit and machine-checkable. **Supports (`informed_by`)** — "from materially rests on to": a decision points at the fact, test, log or conversation it was drawn from. The rationale is mandatory: an `informed_by` edge without a non-empty `description` is rejected, in `link` and in batched `create_concept` alike. The support graph stays a strict DAG — an edge that would close a cycle is refused. Cycles imported by a merge are quarantined: the component is closed for writes, shows up in `weak_links` with `needs_merge: true`, and `in_paths` through it honestly reports `null` instead of a made-up number. **`evidence` shortcut** — supports are declared in the same `create_concept` call, no follow-up `link` needed: ```json { "evidence": [ { "ref": "src/auth/session.ts#L42", "why": "timeout read from the code" }, { "node": "req-session-ttl", "why": "the requirement fixed the TTL" }, { "ref": "git:tag:v2.1.11", "why": "shipped in that release" } ] } ``` Each item takes exactly one of `ref` (a file, a git object, or any other identifier; the node already citing it is reused, otherwise a file-fact node is created) or `node` (an existing concept), plus a mandatory `why`. **Git evidence (2.1.12)** — "merged to main", "shipped in 2.1.11" are checked against git objects, not files: `git:tag:`, `git:commit:` (full or 7+ chars) and `git:branch:` resolve to a commit sha via the LOCAL git binary — no network calls, GitHub API is never touched. `check_artifacts` on such an anchor reports the resolved sha; the tag moved or the branch advanced → `changed` with both shas in `weak_links`; the ref vanished → `missing`. Use `git:branch:` only for "has moved" checks, never as proof of "merged". The repository is `--repo PATH` at server start (default: the database directory). Start MCP without a subcommand: `megamemory --db PATH --repo REPO`; `--db=PATH` and `--repo=REPO` are equivalent, missing or repeated values fail before opening the database. CLI subcommands may follow these global flags. The path is pinned into `node_artifacts.repo_path` at the first resolution, so later checks do not depend on the server's cwd. Auto-deriving supports from `why` + `file_refs` exists but is **off by default** (`provenance.auto_ground` in `megamemory.config.json` next to the database) — server-invented supports must not masquerade as agent-declared provenance. **File refs with locators (2.1.13)** — a ref may carry a line locator: `path`, `path:12`, `path:12-30`, `path#L12`, `path#L12-L30`. The filesystem receives only the path (Windows drive letters `C:\`, UNC `\\server\share`, colons and `#` inside names are preserved); the locator is kept next to the row for display and audit. **The digest is over the whole file** — the locator limits the citation scope, not the hash scope: a change on line 500 still flips a ref written as `path:12`. Git schemes are recognized first and are never cut (`git:tag:2026` is a tag named "2026", not a path with a locator). `bench` and `check_artifacts` share one parser (`src/refs.ts`) — a ref means the same thing to both. **Strict mode** — `provenance.require_support: true` refuses a `decision` with zero supports: no `evidence`, no `informed_by` edge, and (when auto-derivation is on) nothing derived. The refusal says to pass `evidence` in the same call — "add support later" is rejected on purpose, because the source of the conclusion is lost by the next call. The flag is read fresh on every call (`megamemory.config.json` next to the db; env overrides `MEGAMEMORY_PROVENANCE_REQUIRE_SUPPORT` / `MEGAMEMORY_REQUIRE_SUPPORT`, `1|0`). Other kinds, `link` and reads are unaffected. **`provenance_trace` / `provenance_audit`** — walk `informed_by` in one direction: `ancestry` ("what does this rest on") or `impact` ("what rests on it"). The completeness contract is honest about what it did not show: `total_within_depth` counts nodes within `depth`; the reason for stopping is `truncated_by: depth | nodes | scan | null`; `in_paths` is the number of paths in the shown subgraph, capped and flagged (`in_paths_capped`) rather than exaggerated; the scan budget `max_scan_nodes` (default 5000) bounds both output and work (`total_exact: false` when it fires). Weak links come first — refuted/abandoned nodes, cycle components, edges without rationale, decisions with `no_support` / `missing_support` / only-`ungrounded` supports (numeric `count` plus `sample`, the first ≤ 5 ids) — and the whole `weak_links` block is capped at 8 KB with a `weak_links_truncated` marker. **Removal hygiene** — removing a node that other nodes rest on is refused with a hint naming the dependents; `force` overrides it. Removals leave tombstones, and in a merge an edge tombstone wins over a live copy — a severed link does not resurrect because the other branch never knew. **Anchors vs claims (2.1.10)** — a support created by `evidence: [{ref}]` is an *anchor*: a small node named after the file (`path:start-end`, or the whole file `plans/report.md`) with a template summary ("File-fact node for … — created as a provenance support."). That template is **by design** — the anchor exists to carry the link and its digests, not to state a thought. Since schema v12 every node carries `created_via` (`agent` | `file_ref` | `import` | `auto`), and only hand-written nodes (`agent`) are ever counted as stubs: `stats` splits the support line into `Supports: N (anchors a, claims c)` plus a `Stubs` counter, and `weak_links` raises `stub_support` only for manual placeholder summaries. An anchor is never a stub, and a hand-written template summary is still rejected — the difference is the origin, not the text. Near-duplicates are refused at creation: `create_concept` compares the normalized name (case, spaces, punctuation, ё/е) and the summary vector (top-3, cosine threshold `dedupe.threshold` in `megamemory.config.json`, default 0.92, env `MEGAMEMORY_DEDUPE_THRESHOLD`) and returns `duplicate_of` instead of writing a second copy — `force: true` overrides consciously. Digests and server-built anchors are never deduplicated. ## Facts expire A journal entry is not knowledge: "PR #3 not opened yet" was true on the day it was written and is a lie a day later. Such nodes have no supports, so `support_check` never flags them — nothing it tracks has changed. Schema v13 gives every node an optional `valid_until` (ISO-8601, UTC): - **When to set it** — any statement about the world as it was: "merged", "release shipped", "PR open", "migration not started". Architecture, conventions and behavior facts stay dateless. The server never invents an expiry — `create_concept` / `update_concept` accept `valid_until`, and leaving it out means the fact is permanent. - **What happens on expiry** — the node drops out of `understand` answers (`meta.stale_excluded` counts how many were hidden); `include_stale: true` returns them marked `expired: true`. Nothing is deleted: the node stays in the graph, in `get_concept`, in history — it just stops masquerading as current knowledge. - **How it surfaces** — `provenance_trace` does not cut the chain at an expired predecessor: it is still traversed and counted, but marked `expired` and reported as a weak link. `stats` shows an `Expired` line; `doctor` warns when more than 10% of active nodes are past their date. - **Superseded is not expired** — the `valid_until` written by `supersedes` is a replacement marker on a node that already left the answers through its own status; the expiry filters only apply to active nodes. - **The server warns, never blocks (2.1.13)** — a summary that looks like a state claim (merged/released/pending, a PR number, a semver, a date) without `valid_until` gets a `state_claim_without_expiry` warning in the tool response; an expiry already in the past gets `expired_on_create`. The node is still written — setting the date is the agent's call, the server does not invent one. `kind=digest` is exempt. - **Manual expiry (2.1.13)** — `megamemory expire --ids a,b --until 2027-01-01 [--apply]` (or `--until past` = yesterday) sets `valid_until` on existing nodes; dry-run by default, one unknown id refuses the whole batch, every application writes a `timeline` entry. Cleanup candidates on a live base: run it on a copy, keep useful content by rewriting it instead of expiring. --- ## Measuring the benefit Is the memory actually useful? Don't argue — measure: `megamemory bench` tells you in numbers whether **orientation via the graph is cheaper than the alternative**, and how often it points at the right nodes. Three baselines, one flag: ```bash # vs reading the file_refs files of the found nodes (default) megamemory bench --db .megamemory/knowledge.db --questions q.jsonl --baseline files # vs token-economy-ts 1.1.0 text search: run from the analyzed project's root # Replace the executable/script paths below with their absolute local paths. megamemory bench --db "" --questions q.jsonl --baseline te \ --te-exec "C:/Program Files/nodejs/node.exe" \ --te-arg "C:/p/agent-skills/skills/token-economy-ts/scripts/code-searcher.js" \ --te-arg "query={query}" --te-arg "root=." --te-arg "ext=.ts,.tsx,.js,.jsx,.mjs,.cjs" # both ratios side by side: where memory wins, where the structural tool is the right call megamemory bench --db .megamemory/knowledge.db --questions q.jsonl --baseline both ``` `lang` groups results; it does not dispatch a skill. `root`/`--ref-root` resolve file references and do not change runner cwd. Preset token counts bypass the runner; precedence is preset → structured runner → per-question shell → global shell. Shell templates are trusted advanced input, especially on Windows. Graph path requires two endpoints, not a natural-language query: ```text node "C:/p/agent-skills/skills/token-economy-ts/scripts/graph-tool.js" op=path from=src/a.ts to=src/b.ts root=. python -I "C:/p/agent-skills/skills/token-economy-py/scripts/te.py" search "apply_catalog" --root "" node "C:/p/agent-skills/skills/token-economy-har/har.js" search "AbsentNeedle" --file "" --json ``` PY search returns UTF-8 text, not JSON. HAR complete no-match returns its JSON payload with exit1 and empty stderr; parse/regex/read errors exit2 instead. TS 1.1.0 / PY 1.2.1 / HAR 1.0.1 use separate CLI/output contracts; use the script from the source/staging package or an explicitly updated installation. A complete expected no-match is valid; errors, absent payloads and truncation are not proof of quality or a measurable advantage. `graph_metric=retrieval_wire_without_instructions` estimates the MCP content wrapper around retrieval (including `next`), **without MCP instructions metadata**. It is not exactly the default MCP response and not whole-task telemetry (`economy_status=not_measured`). No fixed token correction is applied. `ratio > 1` means the graph is cheaper; `ratio < 1` means the baseline is cheaper: 200 / 100 = 2, 100 / 200 = 0.5. For quality-gated TE comparisons, add `expected_outcome`, `expect_nodes`, `quality_contract` and `expected_te_refs`/`expected_te_symbols`/`expected_te_edges` to the dataset; see [the explicit adapter schemas](docs/bench-protocol.md#quality-and-completeness). `quality_ratio_te` and its median include only correct complete live pairs; legacy `ratio_te`/token totals are **raw retrieval costs**, not evidence of benefit. Preset counts are not live; malformed/error/absent payloads (even exit0) are never eligible. A complete valid expected negative passes quality and can be compared when both costs are positive. The report counts failures/unknowns over all questions. The runner captures at most 16 MiB of stdout/stderr each, counts all emitted bytes, and marks truncation; a partial prefix has no exact token cost or ratio. `ratio = baseline_tokens / graph_tokens` — but never read it without `hit_rate` (did the expected nodes surface in the top-10): a cheap but wrong answer is not savings. Questions where the graph lost (`ratio < 1`) are printed, not hidden. And the honest caveat the command itself prints: **bench measures the cost of orientation, not the quality of the answer — fewer tokens with worse quality is not a saving.** For a live agent A/B comparison, see [docs/bench-protocol.md](docs/bench-protocol.md). ### How to read the numbers - **`hit_rate` vs `hit_rate@1`.** `hit_rate` counts a question as a hit when any expected node surfaced anywhere in the top-10; `hit_rate@1` counts only when the best expected node ranked **first** (the `rank` column shows that position). `hit_rate@1 ≤ hit_rate` always — a rank-6 "hit" is a much weaker answer than a rank-1 one, and reading only the top-10 number overstates the graph. - **Why `hit_rate@1` can drop after you add knowledge.** Supports (the `informed_by` facts behind a decision) contain the query terms verbatim — "EBUSY", "two-batch race" — and compete with the decision itself in search, pushing it off rank 1: the agent asks "why" and gets a fact fragment instead of the decision the fact belongs to. Since 2.1.7 such **nested supports** leave the top level and fold under their decision (the `supports` field on the node, depth 1), so adding knowledge no longer sinks `hit_rate@1`; in bench a nested support counts as found at its decision's rank, and `meta.supports_inlined` reports how many nodes were folded. When the decision did not make the output, its support stays a standalone fact on the top level — knowledge is regrouped, never hidden. - **`r(files)` vs `r(files-top)`.** `r(files)` compares the graph answer against **all** `file_refs` of every found node — that reaches tens of thousands of tokens and produces ×50 ratios no live agent would ever pay, because a live agent reads two or three files, not seventy. Run with `--files-top 3` and read `r(files-top)`: the baseline over the first three unique files in the output order (the order of found nodes, not the alphabet). `r(files-top) ≤ r(files)` always; when `N` exceeds the number of unique files they coincide. - **`refs: resolved N/M (roots: …)`** — how many of the `M` unique `file_refs` pointed at files that actually exist. Refs with line suffixes (`src/db.ts:9`, `src/db.ts:605-643`) resolve to the same file as `src/db.ts`; a ref is tried against the question's `ref_roots`, then `--ref-root PATH` (repeatable), then the git root, then the cwd — the first hit wins. A high `missing:N` in the notes means the roots don't match how the refs were written; add a `--ref-root` instead of ignoring the misses. - **`unknown_supports`** — found **decisions** with no confirmed support snapshot: the graph points at a decision, but nobody has verified yet that its justification still holds (per-question `unk:N` note, ids in the summary). It is a to-confirm queue, not an error; `stale_hits` (`st:N`) is the same for decisions whose confirmed support has since drifted. - **`cold-start`** — the first question paid the embedding model load (its time is far above the median of the rest). The summary prints `warmup: …s (model load, excluded from median time)` next to the median without it; neither number is hidden. --- ## Install Requires Node.js >= 20.10 (raised from 18: sharp, pulled in by the embedding pipeline, uses `import ... with { type: "json" }`, which Node 20.9 cannot parse; dev toolchain — vite/vitest — needs >= 20.19). For Russian-only projects a much smaller model (`cointegrated/rubert-tiny2`, 312-dim) works after an ONNX conversion; the model unloads after 5 minutes idle (`MEGAMEMORY_EMBED_IDLE_MS=0` disables that), and `MEGAMEMORY_SEARCH=fts` avoids loading it at all. The embedding model (~120 MB, multilingual) downloads on first use and is cached in `~/.cache/huggingface`. Install globally from npm: ```bash npm install -g @bloodyeagle/megamemory ``` Or download the tarball from GitHub Releases (no build needed): ```bash npm install -g ./megamemory-1.7.0-fork.1.tgz ``` Or build from a checkout (for development): ```bash git clone https://github.com/BloodyEagle/MegaMemoryAgent.git cd MegaMemoryAgent npm ci npm run build npm pack # bloodyeagle-megamemory-1.7.0-fork.1.tgz npm install -g ./bloodyeagle-megamemory-1.7.0-fork.1.tgz ``` Then either run the installer or register the MCP server by hand: ```bash megamemory install # interactive: opencode / [CC] / Codex / Antigravity ``` ```json { "megamemory": { "type": "local", "command": ["megamemory"], "enabled": true } } ``` The server reads `.megamemory/knowledge.db` relative to the working directory; override with `MEGAMEMORY_DB_PATH`. **Keeping prompts fresh.** `install` stamps every file it generates with ``. The server compares that stamp with its own version on every `list_roots` / `understand` call and returns `instructions_stale` / `instructions_version` / `server_version` right in the response — after `npm update -g`, re-run `megamemory install` when the flag comes back `true` (an agent cannot see stderr, so the signal travels in the payload it already reads). ### Upgrading an existing upstream database ```bash megamemory migrate --dry-run # prints the plan, changes nothing megamemory migrate --apply # backs up knowledge.db.bak-, applies the additive schema megamemory reembed # only needed if the embedding model changed megamemory doctor # health check, exit code 1 on problems ``` The migration never drops or renames a column, so upstream v1.6.2 still opens a migrated database. Nodes lost upstream to the empty-ID bug cannot be recovered; `--dry-run` reports them explicitly. Dry-run boundaries (R-05): a `--dry-run` command never writes graph data, but **opening a legacy database converts it on open** — backup, one transaction (schema, id repair, FTS rebuild, `name_norm`/embed meta backfill), report next to the file. This is deliberate and separate from the dry-run promise: the conversion touches schema and hygiene fields, not your claims. The exporter owns only the files it renders: `export --check` reports extra `.md` files in the directory and never deletes them — prune manually, the exporter has no ownership of the folder. --- ## MCP tools | Tool | Description | |---|---| | `understand` | Hybrid search over the graph. `top_k`, `max_tokens`, `mode: "compact" \| "full" \| "brief"`, `include_inactive`, `include_stale` (expired facts). Every answer ends with the `next` block: `must_read` refs to read, `skip` never substitutes for checking current sources, ready-to-run `followups`, and the `record` line. | | `get_concept` | Exact-ID lookup with children, edges, incoming edges, parent. | | `create_concept` | Add a concept with edges, file refs and `supersedes`; `valid_until` sets the fact's expiry. | | `update_concept` | Update fields; embeddings are regenerated. `valid_until: null` clears the expiry. | | `link` | Typed relationship between concepts. | | `remove_concept` | Soft-delete with a reason; history kept, status set to `deprecated`. | | `list_roots` | Top-level concepts with direct children (budgeted). | | `list_conflicts` | Unresolved merge conflicts, plus `contradicts` pairs. | | `resolve_conflict` | Resolve a conflict with verified content. | | `provenance_trace` | Walk `informed_by` (`ancestry` / `impact`) with honest completeness and weak links first. | | `provenance_audit` | Graph-wide provenance audit: weak links, ungrounded decisions, retention of past audits. | | `check_artifacts` | Hash a node's file/git-blob artifacts (file refs may carry line locators — the whole file is hashed), resolve `git:tag/commit/branch` refs to a sha; divergences surface as `artifact_changed`. | | `board` | Task board; done has total `count`, `returned`, `has_more`, `next_cursor`. Continue with `done_cursor`, optionally `done_limit` (1–100, default 20). | | `trail_refresh` | Refresh fingerprints and return actual fresh/stale state and reasons; a broken chain is refused without writes. | **Kinds:** `feature` · `module` · `pattern` · `config` · `decision` · `component` · `digest` **Relations:** `connects_to` · `depends_on` · `implements` · `calls` · `configured_by` · `supersedes` · `contradicts` · `informed_by` --- ## CLI | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `megamemory install` | Configure an MCP client | | `megamemory serve [--port N]` | Web explorer (graph, search, node cards, Tokens panel, consolidate tab). **Loopback only** (`127.0.0.1`, IPv6: `--host ::1`) — a local tool for a human, not a network service; Граф держит эту связь явной и проверяемой машиной. **Опоры (`informed_by`)** — «from материально опирается на to»: решение указывает на факт, тест, лог или диалог, из которого оно выведено. Рационал обязателен: ребро `informed_by` с пустым `description` отклоняется — и в `link`, и в батче `create_concept`. Граф опор — строгий DAG: ребро, замыкающее цикл, отвергается. Циклы, принесённые merge, идут в карантин: компонента закрыта для записи, видна в `weak_links` с `needs_merge: true`, а `in_paths` сквозь неё честно отдаёт `null` вместо выдуманного числа. **Шорткат `evidence`** — опоры объявляются в том же вызове `create_concept`, отдельный `link` не нужен: ```json { "evidence": [ { "ref": "src/auth/session.ts#L42", "why": "таймаут прочитан из кода" }, { "node": "req-session-ttl", "why": "требование фиксировало TTL" }, { "ref": "git:tag:v2.1.11", "why": "вошло в этот релиз" } ] } ``` На элемент — ровно одно из `ref` (файл, объект git или другой идентификатор; узел, уже цитирующий его, переиспользуется, иначе создаётся узел-факт) или `node` (существующая концепция), плюс обязательный `why`. **Git-опоры (2.1.12)** — «влито в main», «вышло в 2.1.11» проверяются объектами git, а не файлами: `git:tag:<имя>`, `git:commit:` (полный или от 7 символов) и `git:branch:<имя>` разрешаются в sha коммита локальным git — без сети, GitHub API не трогается. `check_artifacts` по такому якорю отдаёт разрешённый sha; тег переехал или ветка уехала → `changed` с обоими sha в `weak_links`; ref исчез → `missing`. `git:branch:` — только для проверок «уехал ли», никогда как доказательство «влито». Репозиторий — `--repo PATH` при старте сервера (по умолчанию — каталог базы). MCP запускается без подкоманды: `megamemory --db PATH --repo REPO`; формы `--db=PATH` и `--repo=REPO` равнозначны. Пустые и повторные значения отклоняются до открытия базы; подкоманда CLI может следовать после глобальных флагов. Путь закрепляется в `node_artifacts.repo_path` при первом разрешении, дальнейшие проверки не зависят от cwd сервера. Автовывод опор из `why` + `file_refs` существует, но **выключен по умолчанию** (`provenance.auto_ground` в `megamemory.config.json` рядом с базой) — опоры, придуманные сервером, не должны выдавать себя за объявленные агентом. **Файловые ссылки с локаторами (2.1.13)** — ссылка может нести локатор строк: `path`, `path:12`, `path:12-30`, `path#L12`, `path#L12-L30`. Файловой системе уходит только путь (буква диска `C:\`, UNC `\\server\share`, двоеточия и `#` внутри имени не ломаются); локатор сохраняется рядом для отображения и аудита. **Дайджест считается по всему файлу** — локатор ограничивает область цитирования, а не область хеша: изменение на строке 500 перевернёт и ссылку `path:12`. Git-схемы распознаются раньше файловой нормализации и не режутся (`git:tag:2026` — тег «2026», а не путь с локатором). `bench` и `check_artifacts` разбирают ссылки одним модулем (`src/refs.ts`) — ссылка означает для обоих одно и то же. **Строгий режим** — `provenance.require_support: true` отклоняет `decision` без единой опоры: ни `evidence`, ни ребра `informed_by`, ни (при включённом автовыводе) выведенных опор. Текст отказа говорит передать `evidence` в том же вызове — опора «добавлю потом» отклоняется намеренно: к следующему вызову источник вывода утерян. Флаг читается заново на каждом вызове (`megamemory.config.json` рядом с базой; переопределение переменными окружения `MEGAMEMORY_PROVENANCE_REQUIRE_SUPPORT` / `MEGAMEMORY_REQUIRE_SUPPORT`, `1|0`). Другие типы узлов, `link` и чтение флаг не трогает. **`provenance_trace` / `provenance_audit`** — обход `informed_by` в одну сторону: `ancestry` («на чём стоит этот вывод») или `impact` («кто на него опирается»). Контракт полноты честно сообщает, чего он не показал: `total_within_depth` считает узлы в пределах `depth`; причина остановки — `truncated_by: depth | nodes | scan | null`; `in_paths` — число путей в показанном подграфе, с потолком и пометкой (`in_paths_capped`) вместо преувеличения; бюджет сканирования `max_scan_nodes` (по умолчанию 5000) ограничивает и выдачу, и работу (`total_exact: false` при срабатывании). Слабые звенья идут первыми — refuted/abandoned, цикловые компоненты, рёбра без рационала, решения с `no_support` / `missing_support` / только `ungrounded`-опорами (числовые `count` и `sample` — первые ≤ 5 id) — а весь блок `weak_links` ограничен 8 КБ с маркером `weak_links_truncated`. **Гигиена удаления** — удаление узла, на который опираются другие, отклоняется с подсказкой, называющей зависимые узлы; `force` переопределяет. Удаления оставляют надгробия, и в merge надгробие ребра побеждает живую копию — разорванная связь не воскресает от того, что вторая ветка о ней не знала. **Якоря и утверждения (2.1.10)** — опора, созданная через `evidence: [{ref}]`, это *якорь*: маленький узел с именем-файлом (`path:начало-конец`) и шаблонным саммари («File-fact node for … — created as a provenance support.»). Шаблон так и задуман: якорь существует, чтобы нести связь и её дайджесты, а не формулировать мысль. Начиная со схемы v12 каждый узел несёт `created_via` (`agent` | `file_ref` | `import` | `auto`), и заглушкой считается только ручной узел (`agent`): `stats` делит строку опор на `Supports: N (anchors a, claims c)` плюс счётчик `Stubs`, а `weak_links` показывает `stub_support` только для ручных шаблонных саммари. Якорь никогда не признается заглушкой, а ручной шаблонный текст по-прежнему отбивается — различие теперь по происхождению, а не по тексту. Дубли по смыслу не создаются: `create_concept` сверяет нормализованное имя (регистр, пробелы, пунктуация, ё/е) и вектор саммари (топ-3, порог косинуса `dedupe.threshold` в `megamemory.config.json`, по умолчанию 0.92, env `MEGAMEMORY_DEDUPE_THRESHOLD`) и возвращает `duplicate_of` вместо второй копии — `force: true` обходит осознанно. Дайджесты и серверные якоря дедупликации не подлежат. ## Срок годности фактов Журнальная запись — не знание: «PR #3 не открыт» было верно в день записи и через день уже врёт. # Bench protocol: measuring what the knowledge graph actually saves

Two instruments, two different questions:

- **`megamemory bench`** — a script. It measures the **cost of orientation**
  (tokens and time to reach the same knowledge) from the graph's own data.
- **The A/B protocol below** — a manual run. It measures the **behavior of a
  live agent** across whole sessions: what it actually reads, how long until a
  meaningful answer, whether the answer is correct.

One does not replace the other (see [the last section](#what-bench-measures--and-what-it-does-not)).

## The A/B protocol

How to compare two agent sessions honestly. The protocol is executed by hand —
a script cannot run it, because a live agent is part of the measurement.

### Setup

- One project, **10 questions**: half «where exactly does X live»
  (orientation), half «why was it built this way» (design rationale).
- Both sessions answer the same 10 questions, in the same order.
- **Session A — without the graph:** the agent may only read files and grep.
  No `understand`, no memory tools.
- **Session B — with the graph:** `understand` first, then files as needed.

### What to record per question

| Metric | Source |
| --- | --- |
| tokens | provider logs (not estimates) |
| time to first meaningful answer | wall clock, noted manually |
| files read | session log |
| answer correctness | manual check against the known ground truth |

### How to aggregate

- **Medians, not means.** One long «digging» question skews the mean and hides
  the typical case; the median survives it.
- Report orientation questions and rationale questions separately — the graph
  may win one and lose the other.
- The result counts as a win **only if B is cheaper AND not worse on
  correctness**. Cheaper but dumber is not a saving — that is the same rule
  `bench` follows by printing `hit_rate` next to every `ratio`.

## What `bench` measures — and what it does not

`bench` compares token counts the graph reports about itself: the `understand`
answer versus the files of its `file_refs` (or versus an external structural
tool in `--baseline te` mode). That is a **lower bound on orientation cost,
from the graph's point of view**. It does not know:

- whether the agent would have found the answer faster another way;
- whether the answer built on the graph is correct — hence `hit_rate` next to
  every ratio, and questions where the graph lost (`ratio < 1`) printed, not hidden.

The A/B protocol measures the **whole session with a live agent**, including
the human judgement of correctness — but it is manual, slow, and does not fit
CI. Run `bench` often (it is cheap and mechanical), run the A/B protocol when
you need proof the memory actually helps a working agent, not just a reading
list.

**Scope statement (2.1.13).** `bench` measures **context retrieval and hit
quality**: the tokens the graph's answer costs and whether the expected nodes
surfaced. It does **not** measure savings across the whole task execution —
an agent's edit-and-verify loop, its false starts, its re-reads — those live
only in the A/B protocol. Consequently: numbers quoted by **external reviews
of this project are not our measurements** and must not be reproduced in this
repository's docs, README, or CHANGELOG as if they were — cite your own runs
or link the review verbatim.

## Quality and completeness

This retrieval metric is `graph_metric=retrieval_wire_without_instructions`: the
estimator includes the MCP content wrapper, pretty JSON and `next`, but **excludes
MCP instructions metadata**. It is not exactly the default MCP response. There is
no magic fixed token offset. TE counts stdout only, not skill instructions or
follow-up file reads. Whole-task economy remains `economy_status=not_measured`.

### Additive dataset contract

No new CLI flags or runtime routing are introduced. One JSON object per question:

```json
{"id":"lookup","query":"Needle","expected_outcome":"match","expect_nodes":["needle"],"quality_contract":{"adapter":"ts_search"},"expected_te_refs":["src/a.ts:2"]}
{"id":"negative","query":"AbsentNeedle","expected_outcome":"no_match","quality_contract":{"adapter":"ts_search"}}
```

`expected_outcome` is `match` or `no_match`. Graph positives require at least one
explicit expected node; every specified node must be present. Negative requires
no graph match/refuted row and no TE result. `expect_nodes` never substitutes for
a TE oracle. `expected_te_refs`, `expected_te_symbols` and `expected_te_edges`
are arrays of exact strings; every expected item must occur. Edges use
`from->to` or `from->to:relation`. A positive TE oracle is required; missing
oracles/adapter make quality unknown, not an advantage.

`quality_contract.adapter` declares the source format (no automatic language dispatch):

- `ts_search`: TS 1.1.0 JSON `{count,matches:[{file,line,text}]}`. Ref is `file`
  or `file:line`; `count > matches.length` is truncated. Count0/[] is a valid negative.
- `py_search`: PY 1.2.1 UTF-8 text `filename`, `N: text`, and footer
  `-- совпадений: N, файлов: M[, показано K]`. Negative must exactly match
  `«query»: совпадений нет (N файлов просмотрено)`. No JSON flag is assumed;
  shown fewer than count is truncated. Refs are filename or filename:line.
- `har_search`: HAR 1.0.1 JSON `{command:"search",total,shown,omitted,items,truncated}`;
  refs are exact item URLs. Complete no-match `total0/items[]/truncated:false`
  with empty stderr **exits 1**, not 0; only this shape permits exit1.
- `generic_json`: explicit test/source adapter, **not a claim that skills emit it**.
  JSON `{results:[{refs?:string[],symbols?:string[],edges?:string[]}],complete:boolean}`.
  Errors/malformed/absent payload never count as a negative.

Four independent report axes: `quality=pass|fail|unknown`,
`completeness=complete|truncated|unknown`, `measurement=live|preset|not_measured`,
`comparison_te=eligible|not_comparable`. `quality_ratio_te` is defined only for
complete correct live pairs with positive finite graph and TE costs; a valid
negative can pass quality and be eligible. Legacy `ratio_te`/token totals remain
**raw retrieval costs**; `quality_summary` counts pass/fail/unknown/error/truncation/
preset/eligible across **all** questions, including excluded cases.
Preset is not a live measurement. An exit0 process proves no payload quality.
The structured runner caps each stream at 16 MiB, measures all emitted bytes,
retains only whole UTF-8 code points, and reports truncation; partial stdout token
cost and all corresponding ratios are null, with captured prefix cost separate.

## Three-mode whole-task experiment

The historical 10 questions A/B above is a manual pilot, not the current full
three-mode acceptance. Freeze 12 independent tasks (two each: lookup, ESM/impact,
architecture, stale/refuted evidence, config/cache, negative/no-memory), with
TS/PY/HAR where appropriate. Run skills-only, memory-only and joint, three repeats
per task: 108 runs **per cache profile**. Cold/warm remain separate. Predeclare
oracle, versions/model, parameters, order/seed, reset and stop after the fixed matrix.
No paid model/network runs are implied by this protocol.

Full telemetry must include input/output/cached tokens, instructions, tool calls/
responses, follow-up reads, retries, memory writes and final answers. Without that
telemetry, functional/retrieval smoke is valid but `economy_not_measured`; it is
not `integration_complete` before cross-project P-18/AS-08 handoffs. Aggregate
paired baseline/joint task costs, repeats clustered within tasks, paired median
and predeclared 95% cluster-bootstrap interval. Savings require quality not worse
and the lower ratio bound >1 for every claimed baseline; incomplete matrix is pilot.

## How to read the numbers

- **`hit_rate` vs `hit_rate@1`.** `hit_rate` counts a hit when any expected node
  surfaced anywhere in the top-10; `hit_rate@1` counts only when the best expected
  node ranked **first** (the `rank` column shows the position). `hit_rate@1 ≤ hit_rate`
  always — a rank-6 "hit" is a much weaker answer than a rank-1 one.
- **Why `hit_rate@1` can drop after you add knowledge.** Supports (the `informed_by`
  facts behind a decision) contain the query terms verbatim and compete with the
  decision itself, pushing it off rank 1. Since 2.1.7 such **nested supports** fold
  under their decision (`supports` on the node, depth 1) instead of occupying a top
  slot; bench counts a nested support as found at its decision's rank, and
  `meta.supports_inlined` shows how many nodes were folded. When the decision did not
  make the output, its support stays on the top level — knowledge is regrouped, never
  hidden.
- **`r(files)` vs `r(files-top)`.** `r(files)` sums **all** `file_refs` of every found
  node — tens of thousands of tokens and ×50 ratios that no live agent would ever pay,
  because a live agent reads two or three files. Run with `--files-top 3` and read
  `r(files-top)`: the baseline over the first three unique files in the output order.
  `r(files-top) ≤ r(files)` always.
- **`refs: resolved N/M`** — how many unique `file_refs` pointed at existing files.
  Line suffixes (`src/db.ts:9`) resolve to the same file; a ref is tried against
  `ref_roots` (per question), `--ref-root PATH` (repeatable), the git root, then the
  cwd — first hit wins. `missing:N` in the notes means the roots don't match the refs.
- **`unknown_supports`** — found decisions with no confirmed support snapshot: a
  to-confirm queue, not an error. `stale_hits` is the same for decisions whose
  confirmed support has drifted.
- **`cold-start`** — the first question paid the embedding model load; the summary
  prints the warmup time next to the median without it, neither number is hidden.

(5 minutes by default), the ONNX session is created without a memory arena,

MegaMemory uses). Remote Turso hosts disallow virtual tables — if the fork is ever
moved to remote storage, hybrid search loses its FTS half (the LIKE fallback and the
vector channel remain). Also, after any VACUUM run `megamemory migrate --apply`
(rebuilds FTS — SQLite does not guarantee rowid stability).

# Read-only database access

Which commands open `knowledge.db` read-only, what to do on a schema
mismatch, and why the reference demo database must not be written.

## Which commands open read-only

| Command | Mode |
|---|---|
| `megamemory stats --funnel --json` | readonly (`PRAGMA query_only = ON`) |
| `megamemory migrate --dry-run` | readonly |
| test-suite accesses to `fixtures/*` | readonly + fixture guard (`MEGAMEMORY_FIXTURES_DIR`) |

Everything else that reads (`stats`, `export`, `eval`, `doctor`, `bench`)
opens the database for writing and auto-migrates an older schema in place.
`serve` and the MCP server write to the database themselves: usage and the
call journal (`timeline`) are recorded on every tool call — that journal is
what `stats --funnel` reads.

## Schema mismatch on a readonly access

A readonly connection cannot migrate the schema, so it fails with an
explicit error instead of reading with the wrong queries:

- `SCHEMA_TOO_OLD_READONLY` — the database is older than this build. Make a
  copy and run the printed command:
  `megamemory migrate --apply --db "<path>"` (run it on the copy; fixtures
  are regenerated with `scripts/make-demo-db.cjs`).
- `SCHEMA_TOO_NEW_READONLY` — the database was created by a newer version of
  megamemory (`user_version` is printed). Update the package.
- `DB_CORRUPT_READONLY` — `PRAGMA quick_check` fails; the migrate hint is
  deliberately withheld (migration does not repair a broken file). Restore
  from a backup.
- `DB_MISSING_READONLY` — the path does not exist.

## Why the demo database is read-only

`fixtures/demo.db` is a reference file: its bytes are pinned by
`fixtures/sha256sums.txt`, and any write — including the invisible ones from
an auto-migration or a deferred WAL checkpoint on process exit — changes
those bytes. That is why a readonly connection is the only legitimate way to
open it, and any real work happens on a copy. Note that libsql 0.5.x ignores
the constructor option `readonly: true` (and `fileMustExist`); the actual
guarantee is `PRAGMA query_only = ON`, set by the `KnowledgeDB` constructor
(see `src/db.ts`), verified by a probe and covered by tests.

# Доступ к базе только на чтение

Какие команды открывают `knowledge.db` в readonly-режиме, что делать при
несовпадении схемы и почему эталонную демо-базу нельзя записывать.

## Какие команды открывают только на чтение

| Команда | Режим |
|---|---|
| `megamemory stats --funnel --json` | readonly (`PRAGMA query_only = ON`) |
| `megamemory migrate --dry-run` | readonly |
| обращения тестов к `fixtures/*` | readonly + страж фикстур (`MEGAMEMORY_FIXTURES_DIR`) |

Всё остальное, что читает (`stats`, `export`, `eval`, `doctor`, `bench`),
открывает базу на запись и авто-мигрирует старую схему на месте. `serve` и
MCP-сервер пишут в базу сами: usage и журнал вызовов (`timeline`) пишутся
при каждом вызове инструмента — именно этот журнал читает `stats --funnel`.

## Несовпадение схемы при readonly-доступе

Readonly-соединение не может мигрировать схему, поэтому при несовпадении
оно падает с явной ошибкой, а не читает чужими запросами:

- `SCHEMA_TOO_OLD_READONLY` — база старше этого билда. Сними копию и выполни
  напечатанную команду: `megamemory migrate --apply --db "<путь>"` (на
  копии; фикстуры перегенерируются `scripts/make-demo-db.cjs`).
- `SCHEMA_TOO_NEW_READONLY` — база создана более новой версией megamemory
  (в сообщении напечатан `user_version`). Обнови пакет.
- `DB_CORRUPT_READONLY` — `PRAGMA quick_check` не проходит; совет
  мигрировать намеренно не даётся (миграция битый файл не чинит).
  Восстанови базу из резервной копии.
- `DB_MISSING_READONLY` — путь не существует.

## Почему демо-база только на чтение

`fixtures/demo.db` — эталонный файл: его байты закреплены в
`fixtures/sha256sums.txt`, и любая запись — включая невидимые: авто-миграция
или отложенный WAL-чекпоинт на выходе процесса — меняет эти байты. Поэтому
единственный законный способ открыть её — readonly-соединение, а вся работа
ведётся на копии. Важно: libsql 0.5.x игнорирует опцию конструктора
`readonly: true` (и `fileMustExist`); настоящая гарантия —
`PRAGMA query_only = ON`, который ставит конструктор `KnowledgeDB`
(см. `src/db.ts`), проверено зондом и покрыто тестами.
